title: Two unprotected databases held billions of usernames and passwords, HVG relays Wired
date_note: The page gives only its publication day; the date of the exposure is not stated.
summary: HVG, relaying Wired, says two unprotected databases held billions of usernames and passwords in total, some with other personal data. Researchers Jeremiah Fowler and Greg Pollock each found one. Wired reports both databases have since been taken offline, and the compiler is unknown.
plain: HVG, relaying Wired, says two unprotected databases held billions of usernames and passwords. Both are reported offline now and who built them is unknown.
exec: Per Wired as relayed by HVG, two open databases held billions of usernames and passwords; both are now offline.
action: HVG advises using strong, unique passwords, a password manager and two-step verification wherever possible.

evidence.quote: Összesen több mint 3,6 milliárd felhasználónév és jelszó van abban a két védtelen adatbázisban

validation.note: One publisher (HVG, Hungarian) read; it relays Wired, which was not found or read.
